Now I have all the information needed for all three questions. Here are the precise answers:

---

**h01**: S3 presign runner (`s3presign.Runner`) -- every 12 hours (`time.Hour * 12`, line 27 of `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`) -- wired at `server/server.go:162` where it is created and line 169 where `Run` is launched in a goroutine.

Component: `s3presign.Runner` (the `CheckAndPresign` method re-signs S3 attachment URLs before they expire)
Schedule: every 12 hours (const `runnerInterval` at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`)
Wiring site: `server/server.go:162-169`

Format: **s3presign.Runner -- every 12 hours -- server/server.go:162**

---

**h02**: The outbound delivery executes in `webhook.Post` at `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`. SSRF protection is implemented via `safeDialContext` (same file, line 59) which resolves hostnames and rejects reserved/private IPs, plus `ValidateURL` at `/bench/home/work/internal/webhook/validate.go:62` which validates URLs at registration time. The reserved CIDR list is at `validate.go:14-23`.

Format: **delivery function -- `webhook.Post` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`; protection mechanism -- `safeDialContext` + `isReservedIP` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go:59` and `ValidateURL` at `internal/webhook/validate.go:62`**

---

**h03**: The provider abstraction is defined in package `internal/idp` (`/bench/home/work/internal/idp/idp.go`) which declares the `IdentityProviderUserInfo` struct. The concrete protocol implementation that ships is OAuth2, in package `internal/idp/oauth2` (`/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`).

Format: **abstraction package: `internal/idp`; implementation package: `internal/idp/oauth2`**
